synthesis: The construction has three rate budgets with different roles: prime-adic common-divisor saving reduces normalization cost, saddle geometry controls exponential smallness of the linear form, and a distinct coefficient estimate controls the size of its rational coefficients. Finite-panel irrationality follows when the first two budgets satisfy the source's strict negativity condition, while the dimension bound additionally compares coefficient growth; parameter choices tune these budgets together with the supported zeta range.
source_support: Lemma 1 obtains an exponential denominator saving from prime-wise minima of factorial-ratio valuations. Lemmas 3-6 convert the contour representation into frequency-indexed saddle integrals and give the exponential rate of the linear form under condition (19). Lemmas 7-8 separately bound coefficient growth, using an imaginary root for the sharper estimate. Section 6 explicitly combines Lemmas 1 and 6 in a strict inequality for collective irrationality, and for b=1 invokes a linear-independence criterion whose displayed dimension bound also contains the coefficient-growth rate.
nonparaphrase_operation: This synthesis aligns three independently derived asymptotic quantities with the distinct terms and outputs of the final criteria, exposing a dependency graph from local divisibility, contour decay, and coefficient cost to parameter feasibility rather than merely grouping three estimates by topic.
limits: The finite-panel irrationality test does not itself use the coefficient-growth estimate, whereas the dimension estimate does; the conclusions identify at least one irrational member, not which one. The saddle results depend on condition (19), and exact rates, signs, powers, constants, and parameter checks are extraction-sensitive and require the typeset source.
quality_reason: Accepted because five distinct units jointly establish a concrete arithmetic-analytic dependency chain and the final section actually performs the relevant rate comparisons. The synthesis corrects the candidate's potentially over-broad three-budget phrasing by preserving the source's distinction between the finite-panel and dimension criteria.

synthesis: Reflection parity filters the differentiated integer sum to a rational linear form supported on a bounded band of odd zeta values, and the cotangent residue kernel then preserves that already filtered sum while changing it into a vertical contour integral. Thus later contour deformation and saddle estimation operate on a representation whose arithmetic support was fixed before the asymptotic analysis.
source_support: The analytic-construction span defines the odd rational function, forms the differentiated sum, and states that partial fractions together with oddness yield a linear form over odd s with b<s<a+b. The next span gives the normalized cotangent derivative the matching order-b principal part at every integer, identifies its residues with the differentiated samples, and uses decay on the other rectangle sides to obtain the vertical contour representation of the same I.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis composes two representation changes and tracks an invariant across them: reflection and partial fractions restrict zeta support, while residue calculus transports the resulting discrete linear form into contour geometry without reopening that support.
limits: The cotangent kernel preserves rather than causes the odd-zeta filter. These spans do not establish saddle dominance, exponential decay, nonvanishing, or irrationality. Exact cancellation formulas, derivative normalization, signs, orientations, product ranges, and contour coordinates are extraction-sensitive and require PDF verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because the two units jointly support a concrete preservation mechanism across discrete arithmetic and contour representations that neither unit supplies alone. The wording avoids attributing parity selection to the residue kernel and retains the source's formula-risk boundary.

synthesis: The source uses related algebraic saddle data for two different asymptotic tasks: frequency-indexed saddles and their contour geometry determine the exponential size of the linear form, while auxiliary horizontal integrals select a minimal-modulus imaginary root to sharpen the exponential bound on its coefficients. Their eventual comparison therefore measures usefulness against representation cost rather than duplicating one asymptotic estimate.
source_support: Lemma 3 separates phase and amplitude, decomposes the original contour integral into finitely many frequency-indexed integrals, and turns stationarity into a polynomial-root problem. Under condition (19), Lemmas 4-6 classify admissible saddles, justify contour choices, and select the root governing the rate of I_n. Lemmas 7-8 first give a common coefficient bound and then use auxiliary horizontal integrals and a minimal-modulus imaginary root of the same polynomial to sharpen it, with equality only for the highest indexed coefficient.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis compares how the same phase/root machinery is re-routed through different contour representations and root-selection rules, assigning one geometry to decay of the target linear form and the other to growth of the coefficients that encode it.
limits: This distinction is conditional on the source's root hypothesis and contour arguments and should not be generalized to other irrationality methods. For b>1 the linear-form rate is a limsup; most coefficient rates are upper bounds, not exact asymptotics. Branches, contours, root notation, powers, and rate formulas require typeset verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because three distinct units jointly document two noninterchangeable saddle selections tied to different quantities, providing a concrete comparison unavailable from either asymptotic strand alone. The synthesis preserves the hypotheses and does not promote upper bounds to equalities.

synthesis: The theorem panels are obtained by parameter design: the chosen odd parameters determine the supported interval of odd zeta values and are simultaneously required to make the denominator-saving and linear-form-decay inequality strictly favorable. This converts one collective linear form into an at-least-one-irrational statement for each finite panel, deliberately losing the identity of the irrational member.
source_support: The main-results span states the finite collections and the general odd-b family only as collective at-least-one-irrational conclusions, and maps the proof to saddle, denominator, coefficient, and final-deduction sections. Section 6 states the criterion for odd s with b<s<a+b, substitutes explicit triples (a,b,c) for the listed panels, and chooses a=7b and c=3 for the general family before verifying the required strict inequality.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis maps parameter substitutions through both support bounds and a feasibility inequality to explain how a general linear-form construction specializes into theorem families, while tracking the information lost when the criterion returns only a collective conclusion.
limits: The selected parameters prove only that some member of each panel is irrational, not which member. The theorem-map span alone does not establish the parameter-to-support mechanism; that bridge comes from Section 6. Exact panel endpoints, numerical root approximations, constants, and inequality checks are formula-sensitive and require verification in the typeset article.
quality_reason: Accepted because the theorem statements and final parameter-selection span jointly support a concrete specialization mechanism rather than a generic thematic link. The synthesis retains the collective nature of the conclusion and the division of evidentiary labor between the two units.
